question.text: An iron rocket fragment initially at<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mo>-</mo><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> enters the earth's atmosphere almost horizontally and quickly fuses completely in atmospheric friction. Specific heat of iron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>11</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kcal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, its melting point is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1535</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and the latent heat of fusion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kcal</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>kg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The minimum velocity with which the fragment must have entered the atmosphere is

options.text: 1.32 km s-1
2.32 km s-1

solution.text:
The kinetic energy of the fragment is changed to heat. Expressing mass m in kilograms everywher, we have

       12mv2=m30+m0.111535∘+100∘4184

              v2=836830+180≃1.76×106

Hence

        v=1.76×103=1.32 km s-1
